title: भाग A — आधारभूत नियम र प्रश्नको प्रकार चिन्ने
blocks: Task 2 एउटा essay हो। Writing band-मा यसको भार Task 1 भन्दा दोब्बर हुन्छ — त्यसैले यसलाई तीनवटै कुरा बढी दिनुहोस्: समय, ध्यान र अभ्यास।
नियम: कम्तीमा २५० शब्द। माथिल्लो सीमा छैन, त्यसैले उही प्रश्न आउँछ — कति लेख्ने? उत्तर: २६०–२९०, बढीमा ३००।
कहिल्यै २५० भन्दा कम होइन। २४८ शब्द भए पनि penalty लाग्छ।
३२० भन्दा बढी लेख्दा कुनै फाइदा छैन; गल्ती मात्र बढ्छ र revision-को समय जान्छ।
Answer sheet-को ठाउँमा २८० शब्द सजिलै अटाउँछ। Extra sheet माग्नुपर्‍यो भने बुझ्नुहोस्, तपाईं धेरै लेख्दै हुनुहुन्छ।
हरेक शब्द गनिन्छ (Task 1-का नियम हेर्नुहोस्)। प्रश्नबाट सारेका शब्दहरूले तपाईंको सीप देखाउँदैनन्।
परीक्षा हलमा शब्द नगन्नुहोस्; आफ्नो हस्तलेखमा २८० शब्दले कति लाइन लिन्छ (प्रायः १८–२२) भन्ने पहिले नै थाहा पाउनुहोस्।
प्रश्न दुई पटक पढ्ने, underline गर्ने, प्रकार छुट्याउने, brainstorm, plan

Question paper आफैँले ४० मिनेट भन्छ; कसैलाई अलि बढी लाग्छ, कसैलाई कम, तर औसतमा ४० मै राख्नुहोस्। Plan नगर्नेको paragraph बाटो बिराउँछ; revision नगर्नेले ५ वटा सजिला गल्ती छोड्छ। दुवैले आधा band घटाउँछन्।

Standard ५ वटा हो: Introduction · Body 1 · Body 2 · Body 3 · Conclusion। Idea राम्रोसँग develop गरिएको छ भने ४ वटा (२ वटा body paragraph) लेख्दा पनि उही score आउँछ। के चल्दैन: एउटै ठूलो block, वा दुई–दुई लाइनका ७–८ वटा टुक्रा।
कुनै पनि paragraph-मा **heading**, bullet वा numbering नराख्नुहोस्। पूरा वाक्य, पूरा paragraph।

Task 2-का topic सधैँ समाजसँग सम्बन्धित हुन्छन्: शिक्षा, काम, technology, वातावरण, स्वास्थ्य, परिवार, अपराध, शहर, media, संस्कृति — तिनका कारण, परिणाम, समाधान, फाइदा र बेफाइदा, वा कुनै विवादित विषयमा आफ्नो opinion। कुनै पनि topic-का लागि विशेष ज्ञान चाहिँदैन, त्यसैले डराउनुपर्ने केही छैन। तर सामान्य ज्ञान भने पक्कै चाहिन्छ — हरेक point-लाई कारण र उदाहरण चाहिन्छ, र ती तपाईंकै दिमागबाट आउनुपर्छ। त्यसैले हरेक दिन अंग्रेजीमा समाचार पढ्नु वास्तवमा परीक्षाकै तयारी हो।
Paper test-मा pencil-ले लेख्नुहोस् — सच्याउन सजिलो हुन्छ।
पूरा प्रश्न दुई पटक पढ्नुहोस्। विषयका शब्द (topic) र निर्देशनका शब्द (के गर्नुपर्छ) छुट्टाछुट्टै underline गर्नुहोस्।
प्रश्नको प्रकार छुट्याउनुहोस् (तल हेर्नुहोस्)। Conclusion-मा के जान्छ भन्ने यसैले तय गर्छ।
Question paper-को खाली ठाउँमा brainstorm गर्नुहोस् — हरेक पक्षका लागि ३–५ वटा point। Essay-को ७०% काम यही हो; IELTS आफैँ भन्छ brainstorm-लाई ८ मिनेटसम्म दिन सकिन्छ, हामी भन्छौँ कम्तीमा ५ मिनेट।
अन्त्यमा ३–५ मिनेट आफ्नो लेखाइ जाँच्नुहोस् — आफ्ना धेरै गल्ती आफैँ समात्नुहुनेछ।
Synonym भएको ठाउँमा प्रश्नकै शब्द दोहोर्‍याउनु।

असम्बन्धित कुरा लेख्नु। एउटा वाक्य माफ हुन्छ, एउटा paragraph होइन — मानौँ topic बालबालिकाको शिक्षा हो: वयस्क शिक्षाबारे एक–दुई वाक्य लेख्न सक्नुहुन्छ, तर पूरै paragraph लेख्नुभयो भने त्यो irrelevant मानिन्छ र score घट्छ।

पक्का नभएको grammar वा शब्द प्रयोग गर्नु। फरक–फरक वाक्य र कम चलेका vocabulary प्रयोग गर्न खोज्दा गल्ती गर्नुभयो भने score बढ्नुको सट्टा सामान्यतया पाउने भन्दा पनि तल झर्छ। आत्मविश्वास छ भने मात्र; नत्र "I eat rice" जस्ता सरल वाक्य लेख्नुहोस् र linking word-ले जोड्नुहोस्।
घोकेका essay। Examiner-ले एक नजरमै चिन्छन्, र घोकेको essay वास्तविक प्रश्नसँग कहिल्यै मिल्दैन।
सार: essay-लाई राम्रोसँग मिलाउनुहोस् र आफ्नो दृष्टिकोण स्पष्ट रूपमा राख्नुहोस्। राम्रो score यसैले ल्याउँछ।
प्रश्नको प्रकार चिन्ने — सबैभन्दा महत्त्वपूर्ण सीप
हरेक Task 2 प्रश्नका दुई भाग हुन्छन्:

Instruction — विषयसँग तपाईंले के गर्नुपर्छ। यो प्रायः अन्तिम वाक्य हुन्छ। (त्यसको तल रहने सामान्य निर्देशन — "Give reasons for your answer and include any relevant examples…" — हरेक प्रश्नमा आउँछ; हामीले भनेको त्यो होइन।)
पहिले instruction पढ्नुहोस्। एउटै topic दुई फरक task बन्न सक्छ:

A. Computers have become a part and parcel of modern life. What are the advantages and disadvantages of using a computer?
B. Computers have become a part and parcel of modern life, but their demerits outweigh their merits. To what extent do you agree or disagree?

पहिलो पटक पढ्दा दुवै उस्तै लाग्छन्। फेरि पढ्नुहोस् — पहिलो भाग उही हो, फरक दोस्रो भागमा छ, र त्यही फरकले प्रत्येक कुन प्रकारको हो भन्ने तय गर्छ। A ले दुवै पक्षको वर्णन माग्छ; आफ्नो opinion चाहिँदैन। B ले एउटा पक्ष लिएर त्यसको पक्षमा तर्क गर्न माग्छ।
मुख्य फरक: छनोटको स्वतन्त्रता (freedom of choice)
दुई परिवारका प्रश्नबीच एउटै मात्र मुख्य फरक छ — freedom of choice।
छैन — के लेख्ने भन्ने प्रश्नले नै बताउँछ
छ — कुनै पनि एउटा पक्ष रोज्न सक्नुहुन्छ
सोधेको मात्र — कारण, समस्या, फाइदा र बेफाइदा, समाधान
दुवै पक्षका तर्क, त्यसपछि आफ्नो पक्ष
जोड दिने र नरम पार्ने शब्द (अर्को भागमा)
तेस्रो प्रकार पनि छ — Combination — जहाँ एउटै task-मा दुवै हुन्छन्। तल प्रत्येकलाई कसरी चिन्ने, उदाहरणसहित दिइएको छ।
१. Topic सहितको प्रश्न जसको उत्तर केही point-हरू हुन्छन्
Example 1: Fewer young people are choosing to become teachers. Why do you think this is happening?
प्रश्नको उत्तर केही point-हरूको सेट हो: (1) कम तलब, (2) धेरै कामको बोझ, (3) राम्रो तलब दिने अरू विकल्प… कुनै पक्ष छैन — कम मानिसले किन रोजिरहेका छन् भन्ने मात्र लेख्ने हो। → Narrative।
advantages / disadvantages · pros / cons · benefits / drawbacks · merits / demerits
problems / solutions · measures · what can be done
N.B. सधैँ दुवै हुँदैनन्। फाइदा मात्र, समस्या मात्र, कारण मात्र — यस्ता पनि आउँछन्। सोधेको मात्र लेख्नुहोस्।

Example 2: Tourism is becoming increasingly important as a source of revenue for many countries, but its problems should not be overlooked. What are the problems of tourism?
→ Narrative. Only problems. A paragraph on the benefits of tourism would be irrelevant.
Example 3: Discuss the advantages and disadvantages of children using smartphones.
→ Narrative. Both sides, kept in balance; no opinion has been asked for.
Example 4: More and more people are living alone. What are the causes of this trend, and what effects does it have on society?
→ Narrative, two parts: causes + effects.
Example 5: Traffic congestion is worsening in most large cities. What problems does this cause, and what measures could reduce it?
→ Narrative, two parts: problems + solutions (give suggestions, not an opinion).

Example 6: Children should be sent to kindergarten before starting primary school. Discuss.
→ Narrative. You have to write the reasons why they should be sent; not for and against. (But when "Discuss" is there, it is safe to touch briefly on the other side.)

Example 7: Some people believe they should keep all the money they earn and should not pay tax to the state. Do you agree or disagree?
Example 8: Air travel should be restricted because it causes serious pollution and uses up the world's fuel resources. To what extent do you agree or disagree?
→ Both are argumentative. For or against — your choice. Even with only "Do you agree?" (even if "disagree" is not written) it is argumentative, and you must write the arguments of both sides.
२. उत्तर yes वा no हुने प्रश्न

Example 9: Should companies hire employees for their entire working lives?
Example 10: Is education more important than anything else for success in life?
Example 11: Do children today need more time for recreation?
→ Each answer is yes/no — you choose. Argumentative.

Example 12: Some people think teachers should be responsible for a child's overall development. Others believe teachers should only teach academic subjects. Discuss both views and give your opinion.
→ Argumentative. The two sides in separate paragraphs, then which side you are on.

Example 13: Some countries have banned smoking in all public places. What is your opinion?
→ Argumentative — if your view is asked for, you must take a side.

Example 14: Should education continue throughout a person's life? Give reasons.
→ The answer to the question is yes/no, so there is freedom of choice — argumentative. (The same if it says "Discuss".)

Example 15: More people are working from home. Do the advantages of this outweigh the disadvantages?
Example 16: Many people now shop online instead of in local stores. Is this a positive or negative development?
→ Although the words look narrative, outweigh and positive or negative ask for a verdict. Argumentative — both sides, then the verdict.

Example 17: Reading on the internet is taking over the conventional way of reading.
→ Add "Do you agree or disagree?" yourself — you will see it has become argumentative. If only a statement comes in the exam, it is definitely argumentative.
एउटै task-मा एउटै topic-का दुई प्रश्न वा statement। यो धेरै आउँदैन, तर तयारी छ भने आउँदा आत्तिनुहुन्न। प्रायः एउटा narrative र एउटा argumentative हुन्छ।

Example 18: There are social, medical and technical problems associated with the use of mobile phones. What forms do they take? Do you agree that the problems outweigh the benefits of mobile phones?
→ The first question (what forms) — the answer is a set of points, no choice → narrative. The second (do you agree … outweigh) — there is a choice → argumentative.
Example 19: An increasing number of people are choosing not to own a car. Why might this be? Do you think it is a good idea?
→ Reasons (narrative) + opinion (argumentative).
Example 20: Fewer people are cooking at home. Why is this happening? Is this a positive or negative development?
→ Reasons (narrative) + verdict (argumentative).
⚠ Combination task-मा दुवै प्रश्नको उत्तर छुट्टाछुट्टै paragraph-मा दिनैपर्छ। एउटा छुटाउनु नै राम्रा लेखकहरू Band 6-मा अड्किने सबैभन्दा सामान्य कारण हो।
To what extent do you agree or disagree? / Do you agree?
Discuss both views and give your opinion
Do the advantages outweigh the disadvantages?
Is this a positive or negative development?
What are the advantages and disadvantages?
What are the causes / effects / problems?
Argumentative र narrative-बीचको मुख्य फरक — एक लाइनमा

**Argumentative:** तपाईं जुनसुकै पक्षमा हुनुहोस्, दुवै पक्षका तर्क लेख्नैपर्छ; conclusion-मा **opinion** हुनैपर्छ, चाहनुहुन्छ भने suggestion पनि।
**Narrative:** task-ले मागेको मात्र; conclusion-मा **suggestion** मात्र दिन सकिन्छ — opinion दिनैपर्ने नियम छैन।
1. Many people believe zoos should be closed. To what extent do you agree?
2. What are the causes of childhood obesity, and what can be done to reduce it?
3. Some think university should be free; others think students should pay. Discuss both views and give your opinion.
4. More people are working from home. Why is this? Is it a positive or negative development?
5. Discuss the advantages and disadvantages of international tourism.
6. Advertising aimed at children is harmful.
7. Should governments spend money on space exploration?
8. What problems does traffic congestion cause in big cities?
9. Many museums charge for admission while others are free. Do you think the advantages of charging outweigh the disadvantages?
10. Some people prefer to live in a house, others in a flat. What are the benefits of each?
उत्तर: 1 A · 2 N (कारण + समाधान) · 3 A · 4 C · 5 N · 6 A (statement मात्र) · 7 A (yes/no) · 8 N (problem मात्र) · 9 A (outweigh) · 10 N (दुवैका benefit, opinion होइन)
अर्को भाग: argumentative essay चरणबद्ध रूपमा — brainstorm देखि conclusion सम्म, template सहित।

title: भाग B — Argumentative essay चरणबद्ध रूपमा: topic देखि introduction सम्म
blocks: अब मुख्य काममा जाऊँ। परीक्षा हलमा argumentative essay-लाई सोच्नेदेखि लेखाइ सक्नेसम्म चरणबद्ध रूपमा कसरी लैजान सकिन्छ, एउटै प्रश्न प्रयोग गरेर पूरै देखाइएको छ। चरणहरू क्रमैसँग पछ्याउनुहोस्; हलमा plan-का लागि ५ मिनेट र लेख्नका लागि ३० मिनेट।

Suppose this task has come up in your exam:
Some people believe that private cars should be banned from city centres. To what extent do you agree or disagree?
Topic-लाई राम्रोसँग विश्लेषण गरेर बुझ्नुहोस्। यसका केही चरण छन्:
"शहरको केन्द्रबाट निजी गाडी प्रतिबन्ध गर्नुपर्छ — यो विचारसँग म कति सहमत छु?"

Task-का महत्त्वपूर्ण भागहरू question paper-मा छुट्टै लेख्नुहोस्, किनभने essay यिनै भागबारे हुनेछ। यहाँ: private cars · city centres · banned। ध्यान दिनुहोस्, topic-को बाँकी भाग ("some people believe") लेखाइमा कुनै काम लाग्दैन — त्यो खोल मात्र हो।
विषयवस्तुको हरेक टुक्राको अर्थ छुट्टाछुट्टै बुझ्नुहोस् र तिनीहरू एकअर्कासँग कसरी जोडिएका छन् हेर्नुहोस् — यसले topic-बारे गहिरो बुझाइ दिन्छ:
"Private cars" — bus, taxi वा delivery van होइन। त्यसैले प्रतिबन्धपछि पनि मानिसहरू आवतजावत गर्न सक्छन्।
"City centres" — पूरै शहर होइन, केन्द्र मात्र। त्यसैले बासिन्दाहरूले अझै गाडी राख्न सक्छन्।
"Banned" — पूरै, कि निश्चित समयमा मात्र? वृद्ध वा अपाङ्गता भएका मानिसका लागि छुट?
N.B. यी सबै point essay-मा लेख्नुपर्दैन, तर यो सोचाइले task-को राम्रो बुझाइ दिन्छ र brainstorm-का लागि idea दिन्छ।
"To what extent do you agree or disagree?" देखेपछि पक्कै बुझ्नुभयो — argumentative। अर्थात्: दुवै पक्षका तर्क, स्पष्ट opinion, अन्तिम शब्द आफ्नै पक्षमा।
Brainstorm-को महत्त्व पहिले नै भनिसकियो — राम्रो brainstorm भनेको essay-को ७०% काम सकियो। यसका केही चरण छन्:
यो argumentative हो, त्यसैले essay-मा दुई दृष्टिकोण छन्: for (प्रतिबन्धको पक्षमा) र against।

Question paper-को खाली ठाउँमा, विषयवस्तुको तल, एकातिर For र अर्कातिर Against लेख्नुहोस्। पहिले For-का point मात्र सोच्नुहोस् — अहिले Against चाहिँदैन। त्यसपछि Against-का लागि पनि त्यसै गर्नुहोस्। मनमा आएको सबै लेख्नुहोस्; मूल्याङ्कन पछि गर्नुहोस्।
यस बेला question paper यस्तो देखिन्छ:
2. Unfair to elderly and disabled people
3. Public transport not good enough in many cities
5. Traffic just moves to the edge of the centre

**Brainstorm गर्दा याद राख्नुहोस्:**
▸ कुनै एक पक्षमा कम्तीमा ३ वटा point नआएसम्म नरोकिनुहोस्। ४–५ वटा भएपछि थप चाहिँदैन।
▸ दुवै पक्षमा बराबर point हुनैपर्छ भन्ने नियम छैन।
▸ Task-सँग सम्बन्धित मनमा आएको सबै लेख्नुहोस् — कमजोर idea पनि। छनोट अर्को चरणमा हुन्छ।

अब chart हेर्नुहोस्, कुन point बढी महत्त्वपूर्ण लाग्छ हेरेर क्रम मिलाउनुहोस्। किनभने तपाईंले point-हरू मनमा आएको क्रममा लेख्नुभएको हो — धेरैजसो अवस्थामा त्यो महत्त्वको क्रम होइन। सबैभन्दा राम्रो idea प्रायः पछि आउँछ।
N.B. तपाईंको क्रम मेरोसँग नमिल्न सक्छ — कुनै समस्या छैन; धेरै फरक हुँदैन।
मिलाएपछि — ध्यान दिनुहोस्, For र Against-का point-हरूलाई एउटै क्रम (1 देखि 7) मा राखिएको छ; यसको फाइदा केही बेरमै देख्नुहुनेछ:
6. Public transport not ready in many cities
3. Space for people: parks, markets, cafés
"People exercise more" — कमजोर, हटाइयो। "Delivery vehicles" — छुट दिएर सजिलै समाधान हुन्छ, कमजोर, हटाइयो। "Traffic moves to the edge" — कमजोर, हटाइयो।
३.४ आफ्नो पक्ष रोज्नुहोस् — brainstorm पछि, पहिले होइन
Argumentative essay-मा opinion चाहिन्छ, त्यसैले दुवै पक्षका तर्क लेखे पनि एउटा पक्ष रोज्नैपर्छ। ध्यान दिनुहोस्, अहिलेसम्म तपाईंले पक्ष रोज्नुभएको छैन। किनभने पहिले नै रोज्दा दुई समस्या हुन्छन्:
सुरुदेखि नै एउटा पक्षमा हुनुभयो भने सोचाइ एकतर्फी हुन्छ — अर्को पक्षका तर्क राम्रोसँग मनमा आउँदैनन्।

प्रायः पहिले सोचेको पक्ष सही लाग्छ, तर essay-लाई चाहिने तपाईंलाई के लाग्छ भन्ने होइन, बलियो तर्क हो। Brainstorm पछि कुन पक्षका तर्क बलिया छन् भनेर देख्न सक्नुहुन्छ — त्यही तपाईंको पक्ष हुनेछ, किनभने त्यसपछि essay आफैँ बलियो हुन्छ।
यहाँ स्पष्ट छ: For-मा बलिया तर्क बढी छन्, र Against-को हरेक point-को जवाफ छ। त्यसैले समस्याहरू स्वीकार्दै हामी agree गर्छौँ।
तपाईंलाई लाग्न सक्छ essay लेख्ने काम introduction-बाट सुरु हुन्छ। तर यहाँ हामी plan-को कुरा गर्दैछौँ — दिमागमा — brainstorm-बाट paragraph-हरू कसरी बनाउने। यो दुई तरिकाले गर्न सकिन्छ:
तपाईंको पक्षका #3, #4 — र किन यिनले Body 2-लाई जित्छन्

**N.B.** Brainstorm मिलाउनुको फाइदा देख्नुभयो? कमजोर तर्क आफैँ हटे, र point-का नम्बरले कुन कुन paragraph-मा जान्छ भन्ने तुरुन्तै देखाउँछन्। जुन तरिका प्रयोग गरे पनि body ३+३ = ६ वटा point-बाट बन्छ; थप point (#4) चाहे दिनुहोस्, नचाहे नदिनुहोस्। वास्तवमा **essay त brainstorm-मै बनिसकेको छ**; अब लेख्ने काम मात्र बाँकी छ।

दुवै तरिकाले उही score ल्याउँछन्। धेरैजसो विद्यार्थीलाई तरिका १ सजिलो हुन्छ; तरिका २ अलि परिपक्व देखिन्छ र "discuss both views" प्रश्नमा राम्रोसँग मिल्छ। हामी पूरै essay तरिका १ ले लेख्नेछौँ, र त्यसपछि तरिका २ ले कस्तो हुन्थ्यो भनेर पनि देखाउनेछौँ।
चरण ५ · जोड दिने र नरम पार्ने शब्द (Emphasisers and Softeners)
Argumentative essay-मा examiner-लाई तपाईं सही हुनुहुन्छ भन्ने लाग्नुपर्छ। दुई साना औजारले यो काम गर्छन्:
वाक्यको जानकारीलाई भारी बनाउँछ, महत्त्व बढाउँछ — आफ्नो पक्षका point-मा

clearly, undoubtedly, certainly, obviously, indeed, in fact, actually, without doubt, needless to say, it goes without saying that, the main, the most, the greatest, crucial, vital, overwhelming, solely, mainly, pivotal
जानकारीलाई हल्का बनाउँछ, महत्त्व घटाउँछ — विपक्षका point-मा
perhaps, probably, possibly, may, might, can, could, some, a few, a little, little, only, to some extent, arguably, a minority, unlikely, it is sometimes claimed that, it is said that
Although some shop owners may lose a little trade at first, a car-free centre undoubtedly attracts far more visitors in the long run.

N.B. यिनै शब्दहरू argumentative र narrative-बीचको फरक हुन्। Narrative-मा यिनको बारेमा सचेत हुनुपर्दैन — जहाँ जे मिल्छ प्रयोग गर्नुहोस्। तर argumentative-मा: आफ्ना point-मा emphasiser, विपक्षका point-मा softener — हरेक पटक।
वाक्यको बनोट अनुसार उही शब्द emphasiser वा softener दुवै हुन सक्छ:
Actually, it is not so true. — यहाँ "actually" softener हो: अघि भनिएको कुराको महत्त्व घटाउँछ।
It is the least the government can do. — यहाँ "least" emphasiser हो: वाक्यमा जोड दिन्छ ("कम्तीमा यति त गर्नैपर्छ")।
त्यसैले शब्द मात्र होइन, पूरा वाक्य हेर्नुहोस्।
Introduction बढीमा ३ वाक्यमा, वा २ वाक्यमा लेख्नुहोस्। यहाँ कुनै तर्क आउँदैन। ढाँचा:

1. General statement (१ वाक्य)
2. Thesis statement (१ वाक्य)

1. General statements (२ वाक्य)
2. Thesis statement (१ वाक्य)

Introduction-को पहिलो वाक्य (वा दुई वाक्य) को रूपमा task-को विषयवस्तुबारे, topic-सँग सम्बन्धित, तर task-को तर्कमा नपस्ने एउटा सामान्य वाक्य लेख्नुहोस्। विषयवस्तुका कुनै एक वा दुई टुक्राबाट वाक्य बनाउनुहोस्:
Private cars have become the main form of transport in almost every city in the world.
City centres are where the pressure of urban traffic is felt most sharply.
In recent years, a growing number of cities have begun to restrict private cars in their central districts.

पहिला दुई वाक्यले car र city centre-बीच सम्बन्ध जोड्दैनन् — त्यसैले तिनपछि thesis-तिर लैजाने अर्को वाक्य चाहिन्छ (३ वाक्यको introduction)। तेस्रोले दुवैलाई जोड्छ — सिधै thesis-मा जानुहोस् (२ वाक्यको introduction)। तपाईंका वाक्य यिनभन्दा सरल भए पनि समस्या छैन — गल्ती नभएसम्म।

यो task-को सबैभन्दा महत्त्वपूर्ण वाक्य हो। यहाँ तपाईं कुन पक्षमा हुनुहुन्छ भन्ने स्पष्ट गर्नुहुन्छ — examiner-ले सबैभन्दा ध्यान दिएर पढ्ने यही हो। राम्रो thesis-मा हुन्छ: तपाईंको position + मुख्य कारणको संकेत + (चाहे) softener सहित अर्को पक्षको स्वीकृति:

Although such a policy creates some (softener) difficulties for businesses and less mobile residents, I firmly (emphasiser) believe that banning cars from city centres is the right decision because of the enormous gains in air quality, safety and public space.

"I agree with the topic" / "I disagree with the topic" — यो लेख्न सक्नुहुन्छ, गलत होइन, तर स्तरीय होइन। प्रश्नबाट सुरु नगर्नुहोस्। आफ्नो view नभनी "This essay will discuss…" लेख्नु — त्यो thesis होइन।
अब तेस्रो general statement + thesis = पूरा introduction (४४ शब्द):

In recent years, a growing number of cities have begun to restrict private cars in their central districts. Although such a policy creates some difficulties for businesses and less mobile residents, I firmly believe it is the right decision because of the gains in air quality, safety and public space.

ध्यान दिनुहोस्: "cars", "city centres" — task-कै शब्द दोहोरिएका छन्। यस्तो हुन सक्छ; समस्या छैन। तर चाहनुहुन्छ भने cars → vehicles, city centres → central districts / downtown areas — मनमा synonym आयो भने प्रयोग गर्नुहोस्; आएन भने उही शब्दले पनि लगभग काम चल्छ।
Topic राखेर यसलाई कुनै पनि argumentative task-मा प्रयोग गर्न सक्नुहुन्छ। हरेक खाली ठाउँका लागि दिइएका शब्दमध्ये कुनै एउटा रोज्नुहोस्:

Truth be told, whether or not **[topic-लाई अलिकति बदलेर राख्नुहोस्]** has generated a lot of **[ interest / controversy / discussion ] [ lately / recently / in recent years ]**. The goal of this essay is to **[ clear / document / establish ]** why my answer is **[ yes / no ]**.

उदाहरण: Truth be told, whether or not private vehicles should be excluded from downtown areas has generated a lot of controversy in recent years. The goal of this essay is to establish why my answer is yes.

The **[ issue / subject / matter ]** of **[topic-लाई अलिकति बदलेर]** has been **[ raising eyebrows / a matter of controversy / a matter of discussion ]** for quite some time now. In my perspective, it would be hard to **[ claim / prove / show / deny ]** that **[topic फेरि, अर्कै तरिकाले]** is / are **[ good / bad ]** for society.
पक्षमा हुनुहुन्छ भने "good", विपक्षमा भने "bad"; "deny" प्रयोग गर्दा अर्थ उल्टिन्छ — होसियार हुनुहोस्।

**[Subject paraphrase]** has become **[ a widespread practice / a contested issue / a common feature of modern life ]**. While [विपक्षको कुरा, **softener** सहित], I **[ firmly / strongly ]** believe that [तपाईंको **position**], **[ mainly / chiefly ]** because [मुख्य कारण].

title: भाग B — Argumentative essay चरणबद्ध रूपमा: body, conclusion र पूरा essay
blocks: Paragraph-को मुख्य दाबी एक वाक्यमा; paragraph-मा के आउँदैछ भनेर पाठकलाई बताउँछ (introduction जस्तै काम गर्छ)
Topic sentence-ले paragraph-को idea पूरै स्पष्ट रूपमा भन्दैन भने १–२ वाक्यमा व्याख्या गर्नुहोस्; त्योभन्दा बढी होइन
एउटा ठोस उदाहरण — कुनै देश, घटना, सामान्य अवस्था
हरेक paragraph-मा १ वटा; ३ वटा सकिएन भने कम्तीमा २ वटा
आफ्नो पक्षका पहिला २ वटा तर्क दिन लाग्नुभएकाले topic sentence-ले दुवै point-लाई प्रतिनिधित्व गर्नुपर्छ:

Topic sentence: The most compelling (emphasiser) reason for excluding cars is the effect on the environment of the city itself.
Explanation (point #1): Undoubtedly (emphasiser), private vehicles are the main (emphasiser) source of air pollution and noise in central areas, and removing them brings almost immediate relief.
Point #2: Moreover (adding connective), buses and trams that no longer sit in traffic jams become faster and more reliable, so (resulting connective) more people choose them.
Example: For instance (connective), when Oslo removed most cars from its centre, nitrogen dioxide levels dropped sharply within two years and bus journey times fell by a fifth. (84 words)

**[ Undoubtedly / Obviously / Without a hint of doubt / It is undisputed that / It is beyond argument that ]**, the **[ basic / fundamental / main / pivotal ] [ reasons / factors / grounds / causes ]** for which **[topic]** is/are important is/are **[brainstorm-का पहिला १/२ वटा point]**. **[ Firstly / At first / To begin with ]**, … (अलिकति व्याख्या)। For example, … (उदाहरण)। Moreover, … (अर्को point छ भने १ वाक्य)।

Paragraph विरोध देखाउने connective (however, on the other hand, on the contrary, in contrast) ले सुरु गर्नुहोस्। विपक्षका point-मा softener। बाँकी सबै अघिल्लो paragraph जस्तै। अन्त्यमा यी point-हरूको जवाफ छ भनेर एक वाक्यमा संकेत गर्नुहोस्।

Topic sentence: On the other hand (contrasting connective), opponents raise some (softener) concerns worth taking seriously.
Point #5: Shop owners may (softener) fear losing customers who arrive by car, and elderly or disabled residents could (softener) find a car-free centre harder to reach.
Point #6: It is also sometimes claimed that (softener) public transport in many cities is not yet (softener) good enough to replace private vehicles.
Hint of the answer: However (contrasting), these problems are practical rather than fundamental: exemptions for people with limited mobility and a phased introduction alongside transport investment have solved them wherever they have been tried. (86 words)

N.B. ध्यान दिनुहोस्, Against #7 (shops lose customers) यहाँ छुट्टै develop गरिएको छैन — "shop owners may fear" भनेर छोइएको मात्र छ, किनभने paragraph लामो हुँदै थियो र त्यो point-को जवाफ Body 3-मा आउँछ। परीक्षामा चाहिए त्यसै गर्नुहोस्।

**[ However / On the contrary / On the other hand / In contrast ]**, it is **[ argued that / not possible to deny that ] [topic]** has its **[ downsides / negatives / negative sides / drawbacks / disadvantages ]**. **[ Firstly / At first / To begin with ]**, … (विपक्षको पहिलो point, अलिकति व्याख्या)। Secondly, … (दोस्रो point)। Finally, … (तेस्रो)। For instance, … (उदाहरण)।
Body para 3 — फेरि तपाईंको पक्ष (#3, #4) र किन यसले जित्छ
यो paragraph-को सुरुमा फेरि विरोध देखाउने connective, त्यसपछि पहिले जस्तै। यो अन्तिम body paragraph भएकाले तपाईंको पक्षले अर्को पक्षलाई जित्छ भनेर यहीँ देखाउनुहुन्छ।

Topic sentence: Furthermore (adding connective — back to your own side after answering Body 2), a ban frees an enormous (emphasiser) amount of space for people rather than machines.
Explanation (#3, #4): Roads and car parks can become markets, cafés, cycle lanes and small parks, which makes the centre safer and far (emphasiser) more pleasant to visit.
Example + answer to opposing #7: In fact (emphasiser), this is why the fear of empty shops proves unfounded: pedestrianised streets in cities such as Copenhagen record more (emphasiser) visitors and higher retail sales than the car-filled streets they replaced, because people linger, walk and browse instead of driving through. (90 words)

**[ However / On the contrary / On the other hand / In contrast ]**, there are **[ more / many other / so many more / a myriad of / numerous ] [ reasons / factors / grounds / causes / variables ]** why **[topic]** is so crucial. **[ Firstly / At first / To begin with ]**, let us talk about **[पक्षका अर्का १/२ वटा point]**. … (अलिकति व्याख्या)। Then, … (अर्को point छ भने)। To exemplify, … (उदाहरण)।

**केही जरुरी जानकारी:**
▸ Introduction र conclusion-का template दुवै तरिकामा उही हुन्। Body paragraph-का template भने दुई तरिकामा फरक हुन्छन्।
▸ यी template बाहिरका connective / linking phrase पनि खुलेर प्रयोग गर्न सक्नुहुन्छ (Chapter 1-को सूची)।
▸ कुनै पनि paragraph-लाई कहिल्यै heading नदिनुहोस्।
▸ Template एउटा ढाँचा मात्र हो — यसलाई आफ्नै topic-को विषयवस्तुले भर्नुपर्छ; खाली template बुझाउनुभयो भने examiner-ले समात्छन्।
तरिका २ अनुसार body — उही essay, फरक बनोट

यो तरिकामा हरेक paragraph-मा पहिले विपक्षको विचार अलिकति दिइन्छ, त्यसपछि तपाईंको तर्क। विपक्षको विचारलाई उदाहरण चाहिँदैन। Introduction र conclusion उस्तै रहन्छन्; body-को बनोट मात्र बदलिन्छ। हेर्नुहोस्, ठ्याक्कै उही वाक्यहरू नयाँ साँचोमा कसरी मिल्छन्:

It is often argued that (softener) a car-free centre would be unfair to elderly and disabled residents who cannot walk far. However (contrasting connector), exemptions for people with limited mobility are simple to arrange, and the gain for everyone else is enormous (emphasiser): private vehicles are undoubtedly the main source of air pollution and noise in central areas, and removing them brings almost immediate relief. For instance, when Oslo removed most cars from its centre, nitrogen dioxide levels dropped sharply within two years. (83 words)

It is **[ argued / said / claimed / observed ]** that / It is not possible to overlook that **[topic] [विपक्षको पहिलो point]**. **[ However / On the other hand / But / On the contrary ]**, **[ it is undisputed / it is needless to say / it is beyond argument / it goes without saying ]** that **[पक्षको पहिलो point]**. … (अर्को एक वाक्यमा व्याख्या)। For example, … (उदाहरण)।

Some people can say (softener) that public transport in most cities is not yet good enough to replace the car. On the contrary (contrasting), the ban itself is what makes public transport work: buses and trams that no longer sit in traffic jams become faster and more reliable, so more people choose them. In Oslo, bus journey times fell by a fifth within two years of the restrictions. (72 words)
Template: अघिल्लो template जस्तै, केवल पहिलोको ठाउँमा विपक्षको दोस्रो point, र पक्षको दोस्रो point।

Finally, there is a slight (softener) possibility that shops in the centre will lose customers who used to arrive by car. However, it is outweighed by (emphasiser) the space a ban frees for people rather than machines: roads and car parks become markets, cafés and cycle lanes, and the centre becomes safer and more pleasant. In fact, pedestrianised streets in cities such as Copenhagen record more visitors and higher retail sales than the car-filled streets they replaced. (81 words)

Finally, there is a **[ marginal / slight / minimal / slim / faint ] [ possibility / chance ]** that **[विपक्षको अन्तिम point topic-को जुन भागबारे हो]**. … (एक वाक्यमा व्याख्या)। **[ However / On the other hand / But / On the contrary ]**, it is / they are outweighed by **[पक्षको अन्तिम point]**. … (एक वाक्यमा व्याख्या, वा "to stress the matter up," लेखेर सिधै उदाहरणमा जानुहोस्)।
यहाँ तपाईंले पक्कै आफ्नो opinion दिनुहुन्छ (दृढतापूर्वक, कुन पक्षमा हुनुहुन्छ), र चाहनुहुन्छ भने suggestion पनि। Paragraph-को ढाँचा:
निष्कर्ष जनाउने connective (in conclusion, to sum up, in sum, to conclude…)।
तपाईंको opinion — यी दुई मिलेर एउटा वाक्य बन्छ।

In conclusion, while a car ban brings short-term inconvenience for some, its benefits for health, mobility and the life of the city are far greater, and city authorities should introduce it gradually together with better public transport. (37 words)
हेर्नुहोस् — एक वाक्यको conclusion, opinion + suggestion सहित।

**Conclusion-मा के नगर्ने:** नयाँ तर्क ल्याउने · thesis शब्दशः सार्ने (paraphrase गर्नुहोस्) · एकतर्फी essay-को अन्त्यमा अचानक "balanced" बन्ने · प्रश्नले अन्त्य गर्ने · "Thank you" · "Last but not least" ले सुरु गर्ने।

What I have argued here is that **[thesis statement** छोटकरीमा, अलिकति बदलेर**]**. **[ However / On the other hand / But / On the contrary ]**, I cannot **[ say / offer the comforting assurance ]** that it is not without **[ limitations / lopsidedness / downsides / drawbacks ]**.

I have no illusions that my claim will be **[ palatable to all / acceptable to all / easy to all ]**. **[ However / On the other hand / But / On the contrary ]**, I hope that my **[ analysis / exploration / argument ]** can help to understand the matter better.
In conclusion, although [विपक्षको सबैभन्दा बलियो point, **softener** सहित], [तपाईंको **position** अर्कै शब्दमा]; **[suggestion /** त्यसको परिणाम**]**.
जोड दिने र नरम पार्ने शब्द तथा connective-हरू bold-मा देखाइएका छन्:

In recent years, a growing number of cities have begun to restrict private cars in their central districts. Although such a policy creates **some** negative aspects for businesses and less mobile residents, I **firmly** believe it is the right decision because of the gains in air quality, safety and public space.

The **most compelling** reason for excluding cars is the effect on the environment of the city itself. **Undoubtedly**, private vehicles are the **main** source of air pollution and noise in central areas, and removing them brings almost immediate relief. **Moreover**, buses and trams that no longer sit in traffic jams become faster and more reliable, **so** more people choose them. **For instance**, when Oslo removed most cars from its centre, nitrogen dioxide levels dropped sharply within two years and bus journey times fell by a fifth.

**On the other hand**, opponents raise **some** concerns worth taking seriously. Shop owners **may** fear losing customers who arrive by car, and elderly or disabled residents **could** find a car-free centre harder to reach. **It is also sometimes claimed that** public transport in many cities is **not yet** good enough to replace private vehicles. **However**, these problems are practical rather than fundamental: exemptions for people with limited mobility and a phased introduction alongside transport investment have solved them wherever they have been tried.

**Furthermore**, a ban frees an **enormous** amount of space for people rather than machines. Roads and car parks can become markets, cafés, cycle lanes and small parks, which makes the centre safer and **far** more pleasant to visit. **In fact**, this is why the fear of empty shops proves unfounded: pedestrianised streets in cities such as Copenhagen record **more** visitors and higher retail sales than the car-filled streets they replaced.

**In conclusion**, while a car ban brings short-term inconvenience for **some**, its benefits for health, mobility and the life of the city are **far** greater, and city authorities should introduce it gradually together with better public transport.
मैले instruction चिनेँ; दुवै पक्षको brainstorm गरेँ; तर्कको बलका आधारमा पक्ष लिएँ।
Introduction: general statement + स्पष्ट thesis; अहिलेसम्म कुनै तर्क छैन।
हरेक body paragraph: topic sentence → व्याख्या → उदाहरण; एउटा मात्र idea।
मेरो पक्षमा emphasiser, अर्को पक्षमा softener।
मैले अर्को पक्ष प्रस्तुत गरेँ र त्यसको जवाफ दिएँ।
Conclusion: position नयाँ शब्दमा; केही नयाँ छैन।
मुख्य noun एउटा paragraph-मा दुई पटकभन्दा बढी छैन; दोहोरो connector छैन।
अर्को भाग: narrative र combination essay चरणबद्ध रूपमा।

title: भाग C — Narrative essay चरणबद्ध रूपमा
blocks: Argumentative essay (भाग B) सबैभन्दा गाह्रो हो। Narrative essay-लाई पनि उही आधारभूत भागहरू (topic sentence, व्याख्या, उदाहरण, connective) चाहिन्छ, केवल तर्क कम र व्याख्या बढी। Combination essay-ले यी दुवैलाई जोड्छ।
रोज्नुपर्ने केही छैन। के लेख्ने भन्ने प्रश्नले नै बताउँछ: advantages, disadvantages, causes, effects, problems, solutions, reasons।
हुँदैन, प्रश्नले नमागेसम्म। अन्त्यमा suggestion दिन सकिन्छ।
चाहिँदैन — तपाईं व्याख्या गर्दै हुनुहुन्छ, मनाउन (persuade) खोज्दै हुनुहुन्न। तटस्थ भाषा।
उही: ४–५ paragraph, topic sentence + व्याख्या + उदाहरण, connective, दोहोर्‍याइ नगर्ने।

**सुनौलो नियम:** सोधेको मात्र। प्रश्न "What are the problems of tourism?" हो भने फाइदाबारे paragraph off-topic हुन्छ — एक band गुम्छ।
**मिलाउने नियम:** problem–solution essay-मा हरेक solution-ले तपाईंले भनेको कुनै problem समाधान गर्नुपर्छ। Problem: सस्तो fast food → solution: tax वा labelling; "build more gyms" होइन।
Many young people are leaving rural areas to live in cities. What are the causes of this trend, and what effects does it have on rural communities?
Subject matter: young people · rural areas → cities · causes · effects on rural communities। दुई भाग: कारण (किन जान्छन्) र प्रभाव (गाउँमा — शहरमा होइन; प्रश्न ध्यान दिएर पढ्नुहोस्)।
"What are the causes … what effects …" → narrative, दुई भाग, opinion छैन।
Better colleges and training in cities
Schools, clinics and shops close for lack of people
Money sent home helps families (एउटा positive effect)
मिलाएपछि: causes — jobs, education, lifestyle (income-को कुरा jobs भित्रै जान्छ)। Effects — ageing/labour shortage, services closing, traditions; र remittance — मिश्रित प्रभाव, सन्तुलन देखाउन राम्रो।
Intro → Body 1 causes → Body 2 effects → Conclusion (summary + एउटा suggestion)।
General statement + essay-ले के गर्छ भन्ने एक वाक्य — opinion होइन:

Across the developing world, villages are emptying of their young as they move to towns and cities in search of a better life. This essay looks at the main reasons behind this migration and at what it means for the communities left behind. (44 words)

**[Subject paraphrase]** is now **[ a growing concern / a common trend / a widespread phenomenon ]** in many **[ countries / cities / societies ]**. This essay **[ examines / outlines / identifies ]** the main **[ causes / reasons / problems ]** behind it and **[ the effects it has / suggests some measures to tackle it / considers its advantages and disadvantages ]**.

Topic sentence: The most important cause is economic.
Explanation: Rural areas usually offer little work beyond agriculture, and farming income is uncertain because it depends on the weather and on crop prices that the farmer cannot control. Cities, by contrast, provide factory, service and office jobs with a regular wage.
Cause 2: A second reason is education: colleges and vocational training are concentrated in urban centres, so anyone who wants to study beyond secondary school has to leave.
Cause 3: Finally, the attractions of city life itself, from entertainment to fast internet, pull young people who have grown up seeing that world on their phones.
Example: In Bangladesh, for example, garment factories around Dhaka have drawn hundreds of thousands of village teenagers for exactly these reasons. (118 words)

Topic sentence: The effects on the villages are mostly negative.
Effect 1: When the young leave, the remaining population ages, and there are fewer hands to work the land, so fields are sometimes abandoned.
Effect 2 (+ chain): As families shrink, local schools, clinics and shops lose the customers they need and close, which makes the village even less attractive and speeds up the cycle.
Effect 3: Traditional skills and festivals also fade, because there is no one to inherit them.
Balance: One effect is positive, however: migrants often send money home, and this income builds houses, pays school fees and keeps some rural families out of poverty. (103 words)

In conclusion, young people leave the countryside mainly for work, education and lifestyle, and their departure leaves villages older, poorer in services and weaker in culture, though partly compensated by the money sent back. Governments could slow the trend by bringing training centres and non-farm jobs to rural districts. (49 words)
जम्मा करिब २९० शब्द। ध्यान दिनुहोस्: तटस्थ स्वर; दुवै भाग पूरा; सन्तुलन देखाउने एउटा point (remittance); अन्त्यमा suggestion, तर migration राम्रो कि नराम्रो भन्नेबारे कुनै opinion छैन।
In conclusion, [भाग १-को सारांश एउटा **phrase**-मा], and [भाग २-को सारांश]. **[ Governments / Schools / Individuals ]** could **[ reduce / address / ease ]** this by [एउटा **suggestion**].
The main / primary / underlying cause is … · This is largely because … · A further factor is … · This can be attributed to … · One reason is that …
As a result / Consequently, … · This leads to / results in / gives rise to … · The most serious consequence is … · One knock-on effect is …
The chief benefit is … · Another advantage is that … · This allows / enables … · Those in favour point to …
The main drawback is … · A further problem is … · This can result in … · There is a risk that …
One effective measure would be to … · Governments should / could … · This problem can be addressed by … · Another practical step is …
However, not every effect is negative. · On the positive side, … · Admittedly, …
In many countries, more employees are working from home rather than in an office. What are the advantages and disadvantages of this trend?

Plan: Intro (trend + "this essay considers both sides") → Body 1 advantages (no commute: time & money; flexibility for parents; employers save space) → Body 2 disadvantages (isolation; work spills into every hour; not every home is suitable) → Conclusion (दुवै पक्षको summary; चाहनुहुन्छ भने "a hybrid arrangement may suit most" — यो suggestion हो, opinion होइन)। हरेक point-मा एक वाक्य व्याख्या; हरेक body paragraph-मा एउटा उदाहरण (जस्तै Dhaka-को ट्राफिक जाममा दिनको दुई घण्टा बच्छ)।
The amount of plastic waste produced in the world is increasing every year. What are the causes of this problem, and what measures could be taken to solve it?

Plan: Intro → Body 1 causes (single-use packaging cheap & everywhere; weak collection/recycling in many cities) → Body 2 solutions, हरेकले एउटा cause-को जवाफ दिन्छ (packaging → tax/ban on thin bags, producer responsibility; weak collection → invest in door-to-door collection & sorting plants; + education campaign) → Conclusion (summary + कुन measure सबैभन्दा जरुरी)। उदाहरण: Bangladesh-को polythene ban, Kenya-को ban, Germany-को deposit-return scheme।

title: भाग C — Combination (दुई प्रश्न भएको) essay चरणबद्ध रूपमा
blocks: Task-मा दुई वटा प्रश्न हुन्छन्। प्रायः एउटा narrative (Why? What problems? What forms?) र एउटा argumentative (Is it positive or negative? Do you agree?) हुन्छ। कहिलेकाहीँ दुवै narrative हुन्छन् (What are the causes? What can be done?) — त्यस्तो बेला यो वास्तवमा problem–solution essay हो।
दुवैको उत्तर दिनुहोस्, हरेकलाई आफ्नै body paragraph (वा दुई) मा।
Introduction-मा दुवै भागको उल्लेख गर्नुहोस्; conclusion-मा दुवैलाई टुङ्ग्याउनुहोस् — argumentative भागका लागि आफ्नो opinion सहित।
Narrative भागमा तटस्थ भाषा; argumentative भागमा emphasiser/softener।
General statement + दुवै प्रश्न समेट्ने एउटा वाक्य (argumentative भाग छ भने तपाईंको view त्यहीँ आउँछ)
प्रश्न १-को उत्तर (narrative) — २–३ वटा point, एउटा उदाहरण
प्रश्न २-को उत्तर — opinion हो भने: position + कारण + उदाहरण, अर्को पक्षलाई छोटकरीमा स्वीकार्ने
जुन भागलाई बढी चाहिन्छ, त्यसका लागि दोस्रो paragraph
भाग १ एउटा phrase-मा, भाग २-मा तपाईंको view फेरि
An increasing number of people are choosing not to own a car. Why might this be? Do you think it is a good idea?
भाग १: कारण (narrative)। भाग २: "do you think it is a good idea" → argumentative, opinion चाहिन्छ।
Good public transport, ride-hailing apps in cities
But — families with small children may need one
→ मेरो view: good idea in cities
Opinion-मा ध्यान दिनुहोस्: "yes, but in cities" — शर्तसहितको स्पष्ट view। यो दुवैतिर खुट्टा राख्नु होइन; बरु इमानदार र बलियो position हो।

For much of the last century, owning a car was a mark of adulthood and success, yet today many people are deliberately choosing to live without one. This essay explains the main reasons for this change and argues that, at least for city dwellers, it is a sensible choice. (50 words)
एउटै वाक्यमा दुवै प्रश्न: "explains the main reasons" (भाग १) + "argues that … it is a sensible choice" (भाग २, view सहित)।

**[General statement on the subject]**. This essay **[ explains / examines / outlines ] [ why this is happening / the main reasons for this ]** and **[ argues that … / considers whether … is a positive development / suggests how … ]**.

Topic sentence: The most obvious reason is money.
Explanation: A car costs far more than its purchase price: fuel, insurance, tax, repairs and parking can easily add up to a fifth of an average salary, and for a vehicle that stands idle for most of the day.
Reason 2 + example: At the same time, the alternatives have improved dramatically. Metro systems, bike-sharing schemes and ride-hailing apps mean that a resident of Singapore or London can reach almost anywhere quickly without driving.
Reason 3: A third reason is environmental: many younger people are unwilling to add to the pollution and congestion that they see around them every day. (104 words)

Position: In my view, giving up the car is a good decision for most people who live in cities.
Reason 1: Financially, the savings can be invested in housing or education instead of a depreciating machine.
Reason 2: In terms of health, people who walk or cycle to public transport are naturally more active, and every car removed from a city street makes the air a little cleaner and the roads a little safer.
Acknowledging the other side (softener): Admittedly, the picture is different in rural areas, where buses may be rare and distances long, and families with small children may genuinely need a vehicle.
Answer (emphasiser): For these groups, car ownership remains practical; but they are the exception, not the rule. (110 words)

In conclusion, rising costs, better alternatives and environmental awareness explain why fewer people want a car, and for the majority who live in well-connected cities this shift is both sensible and beneficial, even if it does not suit everyone. (40 words)
जम्मा करिब ३०० शब्द। दुवै प्रश्नको उत्तर दिइयो; opinion स्पष्ट छ र अलिकति शर्तसहित (शहरमा); conclusion-ले दुवै भाग टुङ्ग्याएको छ।
In conclusion, [भाग १-का **point**-हरू एउटा **phrase**-मा] explain **[trend]**, and [तपाईंको view अर्कै शब्दमा], **[ even if / although ]** [एउटा सानो शर्त].
Fewer people are cooking at home and are eating ready-made or restaurant food instead. Why is this happening? Is this a positive or negative development?

Plan: Intro (trend + "this essay explains why and argues it is largely negative") → Body 1 reasons (both adults working, no time; delivery apps & ready meals convenient; cooking skills no longer passed on) → Body 2 निर्णय (negative: processed food → obesity/diabetes; expensive over time; shared meal lost — family time) + छोटकरीमा अर्को पक्ष (convenience is real) → Conclusion (reasons एउटा phrase-मा + negative + suggestion: cooking in the school curriculum)।

**Combination essay-मा हुने सामान्य गल्ती:**
▸ पहिलो प्रश्न विस्तारमा, दोस्रो एक वाक्यमा।
▸ भाग १-मा (जहाँ कारण मात्र सोधिएको छ) opinion घुसाउनु।
▸ Conclusion-मा opinion फेरि नभन्नु।
▸ दुई छुट्टाछुट्टै essay लेख्नु — introduction एउटा र conclusion एउटा मात्र हुन्छ।
प्रश्नको हरेक भागको आफ्नै paragraph छ।
Narrative: प्रश्नले नमागेसम्म opinion छैन; अन्त्यमा suggestion ठीक छ।
Problem–solution: हरेक solution भनिएको कुनै problem-सँग मिल्छ।
Combination: introduction-मा दुवै भाग; conclusion-मा दुवै टुङ्गिएका।
हरेक paragraph: topic sentence, व्याख्या, उदाहरण।
Narrative भागमा तटस्थ स्वर; argumentative भागमा स्पष्ट position।
अर्को chapter: हरेक category-का Task 2 student sample — Band 5, 6, 7, 8 — छलफलसहित।

title: Chapter 5-का मुख्य पाठ — सबै category एकैसाथ
blocks: साँचो छ तर हरेक idea एक वाक्यमा · उदाहरण छैन वा कमजोर · "The first / second / third" · हरेक वाक्यमा मुख्य noun · article/agreement-का गल्ती · opinion भन्ने मात्र, argue नगर्ने
स्पष्ट position · एउटा उदाहरण · idea सामान्य तहमा · connective सही तर अनुमान गर्न सकिने · गल्ती थोरै, range मध्यम · कतै कतै सूची जस्ता वाक्य
हरेक idea-मा mechanism + प्रमाण · अर्को पक्ष स्वीकारिएको र जवाफ दिइएको · सटीक शब्द · स्वाभाविक signposting · complex वाक्य सही · कहिलेकाहीँ सानो चुक
विचारको बलियो मेरुदण्ड · प्रमाण हल्का तरिकाले प्रयोग · idiom सटीक, देखावटी होइन · idea-मा आधारित linking · गल्तीरहित
